A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Lizard and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Inspection of all pages supports reliable matching across the revised section structure and relocated material.

before.justification: v3 reports original Lizard benchmark evaluations, passkey-retrieval experiments, efficiency measurements and architectural ablations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains original Lizard experiments and adds RULER evaluation, additional kernel measurements and softmax-retention ablation results.

M1.justification: The gated linear attention, anchor-window mechanism, two-stage training and hardware-aware reparameterization remain unchanged. The added soft-prompt analogy and experiments with different softmax-layer proportions do not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: v4 adds RULER long-context retrieval evaluation at 4K–32K tokens. Alpaca training, the six language-understanding benchmarks, synthetic passkey retrieval and LongBench coverage remain. The new 64K statement is not accompanied by a documented 64K evaluation.

E2.justification: v4 Appendix E and Table 11 add RADLADS as an evaluated comparator, reporting teacher-relative recovery across five benchmarks. Existing comparator sets remain unchanged. RADLADS uses a different backbone, so this comparison does not establish a matched-backbone performance advantage.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce a 50%-softmax hybrid with the teacher described as LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct for RULER, larger kernel workloads, and 25%/75% softmax-retention configurations. Table 11 introduces teacher-relative recovery as a comparison metric. Existing two-stage training budgets and principal hyperparameters are unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 Table 10 extends the softmax-retention analysis with 25% and 75% configurations beyond the previously reported endpoints and 50% hybrid. Existing component and LoRA-rank ablations move into Section 5.4, but the component ablation loses its non-MMLU averages. Gating-design and window-size analyses retain their results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Substantial new result blocks cover retrieval, kernel scaling and architectural tradeoffs. v4 reports RULER teacher/hybrid accuracy of 80.5/81.3 at 32K, GLA/Lizard latency of 18.90/13.80 ms at batch 16 and length 8192, and MMLU scores of 62.8/66.3 with 25%/75% softmax retention. Table 11 adds RADLADS recovery comparisons. Existing main benchmark, small-model, LongBench and figure results remain unchanged; component-ablation averages are removed.

T1.justification: The attention equations are algebraically regrouped with clearer parentheses and transpose notation. Recurrent updates, objectives and complexity statements retain their substance. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced; Local Attention Dominance remains a qualitative explanation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain their contributions, and the new conclusion largely restates them. However, Section 5 strengthens the central recall claim to 64K extrapolation and perfect hybrid retrieval. The displayed RULER results reach only 32K and are not perfect.

C2.justification: v3 tentatively attributes large-window degradation to noise or distraction. v4 instead proposes Local Attention Dominance: local gradients suppress recurrent learning, making a restricted window necessary. It also attributes higher-rank LoRA degradation to possible overfitting. These explanations add interpretation without new mechanism-testing evidence; the stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4 revises the named backend from FlashAttention to FlashLinearAttention and adds its library citation. This changes implementation documentation without establishing that the implementation changed. The detailed hyperparameter table, training-resource disclosures and existing access links are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to RADLADS, RULER and the FLA library. The RADLADS discussion adds positioning around teacher-relative recovery with 40M versus 700M training tokens. The broader novelty argument and relationships to existing linearization methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds a conclusion and acknowledgments, expands selected experimental explanations, and moves component and LoRA-rank discussions from Appendix B into Section 5.4. Appendix organization changes accordingly. The introduction and framework narrative remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 3, 5, 10 and 11, relocates existing displays, and reformats the component and LoRA ablations into single-column tables. The component table drops its average-score column. All five figures retain their content, with limited resizing and relocation within the existing layout.

improvement.justification: RULER results strengthen validation of the hybrid model's long-context recall, while larger kernel workloads and the retention sweep better support scalability and architectural tradeoffs. These provide a limited net gain over v3. The gain is tempered by the unsupported 64K/perfect-retrieval statement, stronger mechanism explanations without corresponding tests, and removal of non-MMLU component-ablation averages.
